'''Ann T. Nelms''' (born 1929) is a prominent African American [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]]. Her research, which involved the study of the persistence of nuclear radioactivity, was cited in reports on [[nuclear fallout]] and human health.

==Life and career==
Nelms was born in 1929<ref>"In Black and White: A Guide to Magazine Articles, Newspaper Articles, and Books Concerning Black Individuals and Groups", Third Edition, edited by Mary Mace Spradling, 1980, Gale Research, Detroit</ref><ref>Blacks in Science and Medicine, by Vivian Ovelton Sammons, 1990, Hemisphere Publishing, New York</ref> in [[Waycross, Georgia]].<ref name="hurray">[https://fultonhistory.com/Newspapers%2023/Pittsburgh%20PA%20Courier/Pittsburgh%20PA%20Courier%201954/Pittsburgh%20PA%20Courier%201954%20-%200050.pdf "Hurray for Waycross, Ga", Pittsburgh Courier, January 9, 1954]</ref>

She worked as a nuclear physicist for [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Bureau of Standards]] in the 1950s.<ref name="hurray" /> She collaborated in her nuclear research with [[Ugo Fano]], an Italian-born academician who joined the National Bureau of Standards as the bureau's first theoretical physicist after a stint at [[Aberdeen Proving Grounds]]. She also collaborated with J W Cooper, a senior research fellow with the National Bureau of Standards.<ref>[http://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.40.441#authors Abstract 40.441, Reviews of Modern Physics, 1968]</ref>

As of January 1954, she lived in the Washington, D.C., area with her husband and one-year-old child.<ref name="hurray" />

==Publications==
* "Graphs of the Compton Energy-Angle Relationship and the [[Klein-Nishina formula]] from 10 Kev to 500 Mev", published in 1953, 89 pp, US Government Printing Office.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=-EgJraKXX4UC&dq=%22ann+t+nelms%22+physicist&pg=PA139 Biennial Report of the National Bureau of Standards, 1953-1954]</ref>
* "Energy Loss and Range of Electrons and Positrons", published in the Circular of the National Bureau of Standards, Issue 577, 1956, 30 pp, US Government Printing Office.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=77kzkFma5eMC Annual Report of the National Bureau of Standards, 1957]</ref>
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=kXa_mfy95zsC&dq=%22ann+nelms%22+physicist&pg=PA122 "An Approximate Expression of Gamma Ray Degradation Spectra"], co-authored with U Fano, published in the Journal of Research, National Bureau of Standards, Vol 59, July–December 1957, pg 122.
* [http://journals.lww.com/health-physics/Abstract/1958/10000/U235_Fission_Product_Decay_Spectra_at_Various.8.aspx "U235 Fission Product Decay Spectra at Various Times After Fission"], co-authored with J W Cooper, published in Health Physics, volume 1, pg 427, 1959. It is cited extensively in [https://web.archive.org/web/20150207073533/http://www.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/488164.pdf "Fallout Phenomena Symposium, April 12-14, 1966], published in the proceedings of the US Naval Radiological Laboratory, USNRDL-R&L-177, June 9, 1966. It also is referenced in [http://www.osti.gov/scitech/biblio/4132950-1jFIrJ/ A Compendium of Information for Use in Controlling Radiation Emergencies, Including Lecture Notes from a Training Session at Idaho Falls, Idaho February 12-14, 1958], published September 1, 1960, by the Office of Health and Safety, Atomic Energy Commission, under sponsorship of the US Department of Energy.
*"Data on the Atomic form Factor: computation and Survey," co-authored with Irwin Oppenheim, published in Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards, Vol. 55, No. 1, July 1955, research Paper 2604.
